text:
emily: Kicking off a quick thread to lock the POC handoff for Carter's pilot. Main asks: success criteria, sanitized data delivery, SQ items (they attached part of SQ-4110), and whether we can support a short burst window for load tests. Target window: 10 business days (ingest + 5k eval prompts).

jordan: Proposed success criteria: 1) p95 < 420ms for 512-token prompts, 2) relevance F1 >= 0.82 on stratified eval buckets, 3) automated redaction confirms no PII/PHI in outputs for the blind set. We'll supply a scoring harness and smoke tests.

carter-cust: Those targets look fair. We'll provide a mixed dataset: 3k synthetic rows + 2k sanitized customer examples. We prefer to keep data in our S3. Can Redwood take read-only access to a prefix or do you prefer presigned uploads? Security leans away from cross-account roles if possible.

infra: Two supported ingest flows: (A) cross-account read-only role scoped to single prefix (our typical flow), or (B) presigned PUT into a short-lived bucket we create for the POC. Presigned avoids IAM changes but requires them to perform the upload. Note: if they insist on VPC egress or private peering, that moves to Private deployment and adds ~3-4 weeks.

emily: Carter also flagged SQ-4110 requirement: redaction before data leaves their tenant. Can engineering propose a minimal, client-side redaction utility for POC uploads? We should also provide a checklist for their security reviewer.

jordan: Dropping a compact redactor snippet that's conservative for POC. Recommend they run it locally and keep holdout rows back for blind eval:
```python
import re

def redact_row(text):
    # emails
    text = re.sub(r"[A-Za-z0-9._%+-]+@[A-Za-z0-9.-]+\.[A-Za-z]{2,}", "[REDACTED_EMAIL]", text)
    # SSN-ish
    text = re.sub(r"\b\d{3}-\d{2}-\d{4}\b", "[REDACTED_SSN]", text)
    # long numeric sequences (cards, ids)
    text = re.sub(r"\b\d{12,19}\b", "[REDACTED_NUMBER]", text)
    return text
```
This isn't exhaustive but meets typical SQ signoffs for POC. We'll include a short checklist: run redactor, verify sample outputs, remove extremely sensitive docs, create blind set.

carter-cust: OK we'll run that and hold back 20% blind rows. We'll also tag rows with category field for per-class reporting (category values: faq, billing, legal, ops).

infra: For scoring we'll use token-overlap fuzzy match (>=0.8) as primary and exact match for structured fields. We'll share the scoring harness (python) and a 10-sample smoke test so they can validate locally before upload.

emily: Pricing  they asked about burst capacity for load tests. For short POCs we can offer a temporary reserved pool with a capped spend. Sales, can we propose a simple commercial?

jordan: Proposed commercial: $600 one-time setup + $140/day reserved node (discounted) for the POC window + standard per-token overage after cap. Unused reserved days will be credited. I'll draft a short SOW clause and include alerting thresholds.

sec-bot: Ticket created: SQ-4110-response (TICKET-6789). Assigned to security@redwood. ETA first-pass answer: 48h.

carter-cust: Timeline check: we'll aim to deliver sanitized CSV to presigned link by Mon COB, Redwood to ingest Tue, smoke tests Wed, and full eval Fri next week. Does that align?

emily: That looks realistic provided no VPC peering is needed. Action items recap:
- @carter-cust: run redactor, create blind 20% holdout, upload sanitized CSV to presigned link when ready
- @jordan: share redaction script, scoring harness, and smoke test by EOD today
- @infra: send presigned flow details + optional IAM role ARN and IP egress list if they want cross-account
- @emily: draft POC SOW with spend cap and circulate to customer legal
Reconvene Fri 9am PT to review initial ingest results. :white_check_mark:

jordan: I'll also attach a tiny local validator (5 prompts) so they can sanity-check scoring before we ingest.

carter-cust: Thanks everyone. If security pushes back on presigned uploads we can evaluate the cross-account route but prefer presigned for speed.

emily: Great, thanks all. We'll monitor TICKET-6789 and adapt. See you Fri.
